row_statement: Conjecture 7.1 of Ferroni, Morales and Panova (the order polynomials of posets of width two, of cell posets of cylindric skew shapes and of cell posets of shifted skew shapes have nonnegative coefficients) is false in its width-two clause: an explicit 43-element poset of width two has an order polynomial, counting weakly order-preserving maps to {1,...,t}, whose coefficient of t is -171571/101393174701. The cylindric and shifted clauses are not refuted.

round2-confirm-G16-opus-20261120-r1/CONFIRM.md (Claude Opus 5.5: CONFIRMED_TIER2, confidence 0.88; own computation through the ideal lattice gives the same polynomial; the conjecture is about the order polynomial, and the Lean endpoint is its literal negation)
caveats: Say 'order polynomial', not 'Ehrhart polynomial of the order polytope': after the shift t -> t+1 every coefficient of this witness is nonnegative, so its order polytope is still Ehrhart-positive.
Only the width-two clause is refuted. MathDB 367613 is the same question and is not counted separately.

The authors tested chains of sizes at most 5 exhaustively and one zigzag family up to 200; no width-two counterexample exists with at most 14 elements (Opus, exhaustive), so the smallest has between 15 and 43 elements; a targeted search finds one in about 20 seconds.

Journal text unread; arXiv v3 is labelled 'To appear in Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society' and thanks the referees, so it is the accepted text. The authors' FPSAC 2026 abstract still states the conjecture as open.
